text:
alex: Heads-up — target change window tonight 23:00 UTC. Need to sequence API -> runtime -> router -> console.

maria: +1. runtime contains KV cache changes, must pin before router rollout.

josh: agree. plan: deploy api v3.2.1 (no schema change), then runtime v2.4.1 (pin kv-cache flag), then router v1.9.0 with route-weights, finally console v0.9.6.

priya: what's our canary plan? small % or per-region?

alex: per-region. start with us-east-1 5% canary for each service, 10m health window, then 25% if ok, then full. If any regression -> rollback service immediately.

deploy-bot: [CI] api v3.2.1 build passed — artifact sha: f7a9c2e

maria: i'll kick api canary at 23:02 UTC. tagging it in deploy queue. @josh can you prep runtime pin config?

josh: runtime pin prepared: config patch -> "runtime.version_pin": "v2.4.1". will push to configstore after api canary green.

alex: note: router v1.9.0 requires runtime v>=2.4.1 due to new session header. if router goes first, we'll get 400s. so strict ordering enforced.

priya: logging thresholds for the canary: error-rate > 0.5% OR p95 latency increase > 150ms triggers rollback. Is that acceptable?

maria: fine. add token-cost spike monitor too (>+20%).

alex: fallback plan: if runtime fails, router will be pinned back to v1.8.x automatically via rollback-policy. rollback commands below:

```
# rollback example
deploy rollback --service runtime --to v2.4.0 --reason "canary-failure"
deploy rollback --service router --to v1.8.3
```

josh: added runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/runtime-canary

deploy-bot: api canary (us-east-1 5%) started at 23:02 UTC — watch: https://ci.redwood/deploys/1234

maria: api canary looks clean at +12m. metrics: error-rate 0.02%, p95 unchanged. promoting to 25% now.

deploy-bot: api promoted to 25% at 23:17 UTC.

alex: starting runtime canary now. will enable kv-cache flag and pin version. josh — please monitor KV hit rate.

josh: runtime canary started (5%). initial logs show warm cache ok, p95 +30ms. keeping under threshold.

priya: we saw a spike in embedding latency earlier — that's likely model shard balancing. if it persists past 10m abort.

deploy-bot: runtime canary health: error-rate 0.15%, p95 +80ms, token-cost +5% — within thresholds.

alex: proceed to runtime 25% in 5m if stable.

maria: router rollout scheduled after runtime 100%. will apply route-weights: api->runtime v2.4.1 first, fallback to runtime v2.4.0 if errors.

deploy-bot: runtime promoted to 100% at 23:52 UTC.

josh: router canary out now (us-east-1 5%) with weight rules. watching 502/400s.

priya: seeing a tiny uptick in 400s from a legacy client — adding header fallback to router config. patching now.

maria: console update is UI-only but will surface new runtime metrics. hold console until router stable.

deploy-bot: router canary shows 400s spike -> 0.9% at 3m (threshold breached). auto-pausing promotion.

alex: rolling router back to v1.8.3 to stop client impact. josh, initiate rollback.

josh: running rollback command now.

```
# router rollback
deploy rollback --service router --to v1.8.3 --reason "canary-400s"
```

deploy-bot: rollback started for router at 00:05 UTC.

maria: post-mortem: client expects absent session header; runtime change requires router header shim. we'll add shim and re-run router canary tomorrow morning.

alex: good catch. we'll keep runtime pinned. do not resume router until shim is in place. console hold lifted after shim validated.

priya: tagging infra to add an alert rule for header mismatch rate.

maria: summary for release notes: API v3.2.1 deployed, runtime v2.4.1 deployed and pinned, router v1.9.0 rollout aborted and rolled back, console v0.9.6 postponed. follow-up: router header shim + reattempt.

alex: thanks all. will update the release tracking doc and post a short note in #announcements tomorrow. :white_check_mark:
